title: Gen-Z Saving Behavior: The Role Financial Literacy in Digital Payment Mediated
authors: Hidayat, A.; Nurhadi N, M.; Nurhidayah; Tanjung, A.; Muliani, M.; Musdalifah
tldr: Analyzes how financial literacy affects Generation Z saving behavior in Makassar, Indonesia, finding that digital payment fully mediates the relationship between financial literacy and saving behavior.
problem_and_motivation: Generation Z in Indonesia shows low saving behavior (56.6% rarely save) and high digital payment usage, but the mechanism linking financial literacy to saving through digital payment adoption is not well understood.
approach: Surveyed 150 Generation Z respondents aged 18-25 in Makassar City who use digital payments and have savings accounts.
Applied Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) for data analysis.
Measured financial literacy, digital payment usage, and saving behavior constructs using validated scales.
Tested direct and indirect effects of financial literacy on saving behavior with digital payment as mediator.
Used SmartPLS software with outer loading threshold of 0.7 and bootstrapping for significance testing.
findings: num: Direct effect of financial literacy on saving behavior was not significant.
num: Financial literacy had a significant direct effect on digital payment usage.
num: Digital payment had a significant direct effect on saving behavior.
num: Digital payment significantly mediated the relationship between financial literacy and saving behavior.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper provides empirical evidence that digital payment mediates the relationship between financial literacy and saving behavior among Generation Z in Indonesia. It demonstrates that financial literacy alone does not directly drive saving behavior; rather, it operates through digital payment adoption as a behavioral pathway. The findings highlight the importance of digital finance platforms as channels for translating financial knowledge into saving habits.
directly_justifies: Financial literacy affects saving behavior indirectly through digital payment usage.
Digital payment has a significant positive effect on saving behavior.
Direct effect of financial literacy on saving is not significant for Gen Z.
limits: Small sample (n=150) from a single city limits generalizability.
Cross-sectional design cannot establish causal direction between literacy, payment use, and saving.
Limited to Indonesian Gen Z; may not generalize to other age groups or countries.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was performed. Domain 1.C (Financial Behavior) was flagged as high relevance because the paper directly studies Gen Z saving and payment behavior. Domain 2.C (User-Declared Preferences) received medium relevance for the self-reported survey methodology. Domain 13.A (Savings Goal Management) received medium relevance as saving behavior is the outcome variable. All other domains were rejected.

limitations: Small sample (n=150) with purposive sampling limits statistical power and generalizability.
No longitudinal data to establish temporal ordering between variables. [unacknowledged]
Indonesian context may not generalize to Philippine Gen Z populations.
remember_this: Digital payment fully mediates the literacy-saving behavior relationship for Gen Z.
Financial literacy alone does not directly increase saving behavior.
56.6% of Indonesian Gen Z rarely or never save (Katadata 2021).
Digital payment platforms can serve as channels to promote saving habits.
